panel: 9, notebook 'Under the hood', lab os-note, footer
what: The chapter dates the 'first append starts at cap 4' stack buffer to Go 1.26, but Go 1.25 already does it for this program. The Go 1.26 change is the one for slices that escape, which is what allocs_m.go shows, so calling allocs_m's slice 'non-escaping' is also wrong.
evidence: Panel 9 (line 215): "That's new in Go 1.26: a small slice that never leaves its function starts in a 32-byte spot on the backpack". Notebook (line 1007): "Go 1.26 added more cases ... which is the cap 4 you saw in panel 9". Os-note (line 1073) and footer (line 1137): "Go 1.26 started keeping small non-escaping slices on the stack, so the first array holds 4 and a growing slice makes fewer trips". Scratch runs with this machine's /usr/local/go1.25.1 (GOTOOLCHAIN=local): slices_grow.go prints 'len 1 -> new array, cap 4' the same as 1.27.3. With -gcflags=-d=variablemakehash=n it goes back to 'cap 1, cap 2'. allocs_m.go on 1.25.1 prints 'append 1000, no cap: 12', the same as 1.24.7. That slice escapes (line 49, keepInt = s). The Go 1.25 notes, 'Faster slices', say: "The compiler can now allocate the backing store for slices on the stack in more situations ... -compile=variablemake ... -gcflags=all=-d=variablemakehash=n". The Go blog 'allocation-optimizations' gives Go 1.26 the move2heap handling for slices that escape. go/ch9.html line 450 repeats 'since Go 1.26' (INTEGRATION_TODO 'From go ch28' asks for the two chapters to agree).
fix: Panel 9: 'Since Go 1.25, a small slice that never leaves its function starts in a 32-byte spot...'. In the notebook, os-note and footer: say Go 1.25 for the non-escaping start at cap 4 (panel 9), and Go 1.26 for the change that also lets a slice that escapes at the end start on the stack (allocs_m 12 -> 9). Fix go/ch9.html line 450 to match.
